description: Guide a student to implement a Simple Moving Average (SMA) trend-following strategy as a LEAN C# algorithm on a single crypto future (BTCUSDT). The student must subscribe to one symbol, create an SMA indicator, implement a price-vs-SMA entry/exit rule, handle warm-up correctly, and produce a trade log. This is the simplest possible LEAN strategy — the 'hello world' of algorithmic trading on QuantConnect.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I have access to a trading engine called LEAN with Bitcoin futures data. I want to test a 20-day moving average strategy on BTCUSDT — buy when the price is above the 20-day average, sell when it's below. I've never written C# before. Where do I start?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need to implement an SMA(20) trend filter on LEAN for BTCUSDT daily bars. I know the concept but I've never used the QuantConnect API. How do I set up the algorithm, register the indicator, and manage positions?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm bootstrapping a LEAN environment for the first time. I want to start with the simplest possible strategy — SMA(20) on BTCUSDT daily — to validate my setup end-to-end before scaling to multi-symbol. What's the minimal correct implementation?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a working LEAN C# algorithm that (1) subscribes to BTCUSDT daily futures via AddCrypto, (2) creates an SMA(20) indicator, (3) goes long when price > SMA and flattens when price < SMA, (4) handles warm-up correctly with SetWarmUp, (5) runs to completion, and (6) produces a trade log with entry/exit records.
required_capabilities: Write a LEAN C# algorithm inheriting QCAlgorithm
Subscribe to a single crypto future with AddCrypto
Create and use an SMA(20) indicator on daily resolution
Implement price-vs-SMA entry/exit logic in OnData
Handle warm-up period with SetWarmUp and IsWarmingUp guard
Run the backtest and interpret the results
ground_truth.termination_criteria: The tutor has completed the following steps with computational evidence (not just verbal discussion): (1) Showed C# code for the SMA(20) strategy on BTCUSDT and explained key components such as data subscription, indicator setup, or entry/exit logic. (2) Presented backtest results with specific numerical values such as total return, Sharpe ratio, or number of trades. (3) Showed trade log entries with actual entry and exit records including dates and prices. (4) Responded to the student's follow-up about the implementation or results with additional explanation, code refinement, or analysis beyond the initial demonstration. Once all four steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
